cousins-in-binary-tree:
# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def isCousins(self, root: Optional[TreeNode], x: int, y: int) -> bool:
        info = {}
        def dfs(n, parent, depth):
            if not n: return
            if n.val in (x, y): info[n.val] = (parent, depth)
            dfs(n.left, n.val, depth + 1)
            dfs(n.right, n.val, depth + 1)
        dfs(root, None, 0)
        px, dx = info[x]; py, dy = info[y]
        return px != py and dx == dy
increasing-order-search-tree:
# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def increasingBST(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> Optional[TreeNode]:
        self.cur = TreeNode()
        self.head = self.cur
        def dfs(n):
            if not n: return
            dfs(n.left)
            self.cur.right = TreeNode(n.val)
            self.cur = self.cur.right
            dfs(n.right)
        dfs(root)
        return self.head.right
second-minimum-node-in-a-binary-tree:
# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def findSecondMinimumValue(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
        vals = set()
        def dfs(n):
            if n:
                vals.add(n.val)
                dfs(n.left); dfs(n.right)
        dfs(root)
        return sorted(vals)[1] if len(vals) >= 2 else -1
